review_notes: Inspected all declarations in CurveCoordinates.lean (lines 1–512), the related PolynomialCharts definitions, and the call site in RelativeAmpleness. The proposed generalization of nonconstant_inv is algebraic and its proof uses only field inversion and the ring-homomorphism laws; I did not execute Lean or verify the replacement by compilation.

findings.excerpt:
lemma nonconstant_inv {K : Type*} [Field K] (c : ℂ →+* K) {a : K}
    (ha : a ∉ Set.range c) : a⁻¹ ∉ Set.range c := by
findings.problem: This lemma is specialized to ℂ as the source field, although the argument only uses inversion in the source and target fields and the fact that c preserves inversion. The result applies to arbitrary field extensions, not just maps from ℂ.
findings.proposed_change: Replace the statement with `lemma nonconstant_inv {k K : Type*} [Field k] [Field K] (c : k →+* K) {a : K} (ha : a ∉ Set.range c) : a⁻¹ ∉ Set.range c := by`. The existing proof can be retained: from `c b = a⁻¹`, use the ring-hom inverse law and `inv_inv` to exhibit `b⁻¹` as a preimage of `a`. The degenerate case `a = 0` cannot satisfy `ha`, since `0` is in the range of every ring homomorphism.
findings.benefit: This makes the helper usable for nonconstant elements over any field, while preserving its simple statement and proof. It also covers the existing ℂ application without changing the intended mathematics.
